source.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Does the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a tree admit a rigorous well-posedness theory comparable to the star-graph case, including existence and uniqueness of solutions in natural energy spaces? The paper says this is plausible and notes partial progress via dispersive estimates, but not a proof of well-posedness.

evidence.quote: By the way a result of well posedness of NLS on trees in not yet proven, although well plausible; a step in this direction with proof of relevant dispersive estimates is given in [26, 27].

accepted.question_text: If one starts from a network of thin tubes or guides and lets the transverse width shrink to zero, does the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on those thin domains converge to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the limiting graph, and if so which vertex boundary conditions appear in the limit? The paper also asks whether those limiting vertex conditions depend on the detailed shrinking process and on whether the tube walls carry Neumann or Dirichlet boundary conditions.

evidence.quote: A first problem is getting the limit of a certain dynamical model, e.g. NLS equation defined on the system of thin guides when transversal size of tube vanishes. It is reasonable to conjecture that this limit should be a NLS on a graph as defined before, but with which boundary conditions? And how the boundary conditions at the vertex could depend on the limit process of shrinking the tubes, guides and junction size? A further difficulty could be the dependence of limit process on the conditions at the boundary of the thin tube, e.g. Neumann or Dirichlet.
They remain open for nonlinear models, where there is no literature

accepted.question_text: Can one rigorously derive an effective quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics for Bose-Einstein condensates on graphlike structures, for example on a Y-junction, starting from an N-body model on the graph and taking the large-particle limit with suitable scalings? In particular, can one determine the correct defect or vertex boundary conditions in that derivation, a difficulty the paper says remains open even for the simplest graph consisting of a line with a defect.

evidence.quote: Being confident that a Gross-Pitaevskii equation realizes the correct quasi one dimensional limit, a similar procedure could be attempted on graphlike structure, for example on a Y-junction; to simplify the analysis, one could start directly from a N-body theory on the graph, and to attempt at taking the N → ∞ limit with suitable scalings. Notice that the main problem, i.e. the treatment of the boundary condition, it is open also in the simplest case of a graph with two edges, i.e. a line with a defect.

accepted.question_text: In parameter regimes where the focusing NLS on a star graph has no attained ground state because the action functional or the fixed-mass energy only approaches its infimum through runaway states, does there nevertheless exist a higher local constrained minimizer representing a metastable standing wave? The paper states this as a conjecture both for the action and, analogously, for the constrained energy under the corresponding mass condition.

evidence.quote: The bad behaviour of the Kirchhoff junction (α = 0) prevents the action with α small, or the energy with a big m, to have a constrained absolute minimum. It is a conjecture that the action has a local constrained minimum that is larger than the infimum when the condition −N √ω < α < α∗ fails, and similarly for the constrained energy with a corresponding condition on mass.

accepted.question_text: For supercritical power nonlinearity μ > 2 on a star graph, the paper identifies a threshold frequency ω* such that the ground state is orbitally stable for α²/N² < ω < ω* and orbitally unstable for ω > ω*. What happens exactly at the borderline frequency ω = ω*?

evidence.quote: The theorem gives orbital stability of the ground state for every ω also for the critical nonlinearity µ = 2 . The case ω = ω∗ is undecided.

accepted.question_text: Can one extend the orbital stability and instability analysis for standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation from star graphs to more complicated graphs, such as trees or graphs with loops, where standing waves are typically not available in explicit form and the spectral quantities needed for stability are much harder to compute?

evidence.quote: One could ask if a similar analysis could be performed on more complex graphs, for example trees or graphs with loops.
In the case of less trivial graphs it is generally impossible to obtain explicitly standing waves, but some simple non trivial graphs can be probably treated along the lines discussed.

accepted.question_text: When the underlying linear quantum graph has eigenvalues, bifurcation theory can produce nonlinear standing waves that continue those linear states. But how can one construct and analyze branches of nonlinear bound states that have no linear counterpart, such as the nonlinear excited states seen on star graphs?

evidence.quote: A second problem is that bifurcation theory allows to identify branches of nonlinear stationary states which have a linear counterpart, but how to obtain branches of states without linear counterpart, which exist as we know from the example of nonlinear excited states in star graphs?

accepted.question_text: Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph asymptotically stable? More concretely, if the initial data start close in the energy norm to a standing wave, does the solution decompose for large time into another nearby standing wave plus a dispersive linear term and a remainder that decays to zero in time?

evidence.quote: A final open and difficult problem is the so called asymptotic stability of standing waves.
In our case a standing wave Φωe^{iωt} is said asymptotically stable if for every solution u(t) starting near Φω in the energy norm, one has the representation u(t) = e^{iω∞t}Φω∞ + Ut ∗ Ψ∞ + R∞(t)
The problem is very hard and there is only partial information also in the case of a NLS equation on the line with a δ potential (see [51]).

accepted.question_text: Do multisoliton solutions exist for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on star graphs, and what happens when several solitons collide simultaneously at the vertex? The paper states that nothing is currently known about either phenomenon.

evidence.quote: Nothing it is presently known about the possible existence of multisolitons, or about the collision of several solitons at the vertex.

accepted.question_text: How does soliton scattering behave on graphs with nontrivial topology beyond a simple star, especially on trees? The paper explicitly identifies scattering on less trivial graphs as open and highlights propagation on trees as a particularly interesting case.

evidence.quote: On the contrary, scattering of solitons on graphs having a less trivial topology is an open problem. In particular it could be interesting the study of propagation of solitons on trees

accepted.question_text: Can one prove an approximation of the post-collision dynamics by outgoing solitary waves for times substantially longer than the logarithmic-in-velocity window established in the paper?

evidence.quote: Another important problem concerns the possibility of extending the timescale of validity of approximation by the solitary outgoing waves.

accepted.question_text: For nonlinearities that are close to the integrable cubic NLS, do the outgoing waves produced by fast-soliton scattering on a graph remain close to genuine solitons over time scales comparable to those proved in the integrable case?

evidence.quote: One can conjecture that for nonlinearities close to integrable the outgoing waves are close to solitons over timescale similar to the above ones.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a rigorous mathematical theory of soliton capture and soliton generation on graphs? The paper highlights these experimentally relevant phenomena as still lacking a rigorous understanding.

evidence.quote: In particular capture and generation of solitons are not yet understood from a rigorous point of view, and they represent a challenge to mathematical methods and theoretical interpretation where perhaps the simple but non trivial model of NLS equation on graphs could offer some insight.
